name: Quantum Pi Benchmark
description: This paper reports the frozen IBM Heron r2 hardware evidence for fixed-position Bailey–Borwein–Plouffe (BBP)-derived reversible arithmetic in the Quantum Pi Benchmark. The evidence is classified P2/B0/R4: formula-derived constants and routing decisions are known to the controller, while reversible arithmetic on the quantum processor produces a hexadecimal digit at a predeclared position. The implemented finite-precision construction classically collapses each of four BBP sub-sums, rounds the four resulting residues to b bits, initializes one residue, and performs three reversible constant additions. The author formally defines this arithmetic, proves a circular quantization-error bound of , bounds the omitted BBP tail, and gives exact rational certificates for reported positions. Comparable first- and second-digit cohorts are included in the evidence ledger. Timestamped static records show that routing choices used compilation metrics before the corresponding hardware executions. The initial six-position campaign recovered the correct plurality for n=0,…,5, with negative repeats retained at n=2 and n=4. Guarded finite-window circuits recovered n=11,17,23 at correct-digit frequencies of 0.539–0.611 while reducing routed CZ counts by 54–70% relative to paired full-width circuits. Exact conditional plurality tests remain significant after Holm correction for the declared primary families.
